security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG generates a logical right shift (shri) or C division (/) instead of arithmetic right shift (sari) for the full-precision intermediate difference in signed averaging subtract instructions (PASUB.B/H/W, ASUB, PASUB.DB/DH/DW). The spec requires diff >> 1 with arithmetic shift toward negative infinity (floor rounding). A logical shift or truncating-division produces bit-incorrect results when the intermediate difference is negative and odd, because logical shift zero-fills the MSB of the intermediate precision width while arithmetic shift sign-extends it, and C division truncates toward zero instead of floor.
security_spec.summary: Signed averaging subtract instructions require arithmetic (sign-extending) right shift on the full-precision intermediate difference; using logical shift or C truncating-division corrupts results for negative odd differences, causing guest-visible data corruption indistinguishable from incorrect ISA emulation

findings.finding: The P-ext packed SIMD averaging subtract instructions (PASUB.B, PASUB.H, PASUB.W, ASUB, PASUB.DB, PASUB.DH, PASUB.DW) are not implemented in this QEMU codebase. The codebase only contains RVV vector averaging subtract (vasub.vv/vx). No TCG translation, decode entries, or helper functions exist for the P-ext averaging subtract instructions, so the vulnerability condition (logical right shift vs arithmetic right shift in P-ext packed averaging subtract) cannot be assessed as present.
findings.snippet: // No PASUB/ASUB P-ext instructions found in target/riscv/
